title: The daily media sweep discards why it failed: the paid-files tripwire (a key outside incoming/) and a Storage refusal both record a bare «فاشل»
evidence: runMediaSweep wraps each sweep in `try { ... } catch { summary.status = 'failed' }` (lines 54-59 and 61-65) and records `p_detail: { objects, tickets, paidFiles }` only (line 70); sweepBucket throws UNEXPECTED_KEY when the candidate SQL lists a key outside the prefix and REMOVE_FAILED when Storage kept a key (lines 38, 41). Nothing logs. AdminHome.tsx:381 renders the run as `${JOB_STATUS_LABEL[run.status]} (${formatRiyadh(run.finished_at)})`, i.e. «فاشل (…)», with no reason.
impact: When the guard that protects paid files fires (paid_files_sweep_candidates returning an assets/ key, i.e. a SQL regression that would otherwise delete sold files), the owner sees the same «تنظيف الوسائط: فاشل» as for a transient Storage or database error, and which of the two sweeps failed is lost. Nothing is deleted (the guard holds), but the one signal that the sweep's SQL went wrong is indistinguishable from noise and the cause can only be found by re-running by hand.
proposed_fix: Keep the thrown code: `catch (error) { summary.status = 'failed'; summary.reason ??= (error as Error).message }` per sweep (prefix it 'media:' / 'paid:'), add `reason` to p_detail like outbox.ts does, and let AdminHome show a distinct text for UNEXPECTED_KEY.
prior_overlap: none (ARCH-13 is about pure-SQL cron jobs recording no run; this job records one but drops its cause)

title: The four owner alerts the in-progress fix migrations add reach the owner as a raw code: the mail renderer and alert_email_data know none of them
evidence: The untracked migrations queue finance.owner_alert('payment_create_refused', …) (20261007100000_fable_audit_payments.sql:221), 'attempt_mode_changed' (:614), 'refund_mode_changed' (:625) and 'policies_reset' (20261007110000_fable_audit_operations.sql:1353). public.alert_email_data (20261002120000_order_emails.sql:191-218, not redefined since) has no branch for them, so it answers `{alert}` alone, and alertText falls to `default: return { subject: 'تنبيه جديد في المتجر', text: `وصل تنبيه جديد (${one(alert.alert)}) يحتاج مراجعتك.` }` (email.ts:590-591); renderOwnerAlert then appends the orders board link for every type (email.ts:598).
impact: Once the M1a/M1b rounds land without a matching F1 change, the owner's mail for «the store just closed because a policy was republished», «Moyasar refused to create invoices (CREATE_REFUSED_401)» and «a payment or refund of the other mode needs a hand settlement» reads «وصل تنبيه جديد (policies_reset) يحتاج مراجعتك.» with a link to /admin/orders: no order number, no HTTP status (the payload's `error` is dropped), and for policies_reset the wrong screen. The fixes exist to tell the owner something specific; the mail tells him nothing.
proposed_fix: In the same round: add the four types to alert_email_data (orderNumber via orderId/attemptId/refundId; `error` for payment_create_refused; `policy` for policies_reset) and four cases to alertText with Arabic text the owner approves; give renderOwnerAlert a per-type link (/admin/settings for policies_reset).
prior_overlap: in-flight: wave A rulings M1a-4 (EF-MONEY-08), M1a-3 (DB-PAY-01), M1b-7 (DB-CORE-01/FIX-A2-03) add these alerts; no finding names the renderer gap

title: The refusal codes the in-progress SQL fixes add have no words in the screens or the refund action: a stopped shipment reads «تعذّر الحفظ. حاول مرة أخرى.»
evidence: Untracked migrations return new business refusals: fulfillment_update answers FULFILLMENT_STOPPED (20261007110000_fable_audit_operations.sql:613) and REFUND_IN_FLIGHT (:580); refund_request answers CHARGEBACK_RECORDED (:930); order_resolve answers PAYMENT_REVERSED (20261007100000_fable_audit_payments.sql:1005). The consumers' maps predate them: REFUSALS.fulfil (admin-orders.ts:607-614) and .resolve (:617-621) lack them, so refusalText falls to `SAVE_FAILED` = 'تعذّر الحفظ. حاول مرة أخرى.' (:652); refunds.ts REFUSALS (:95-105) lacks CHARGEBACK_RECORDED, so refusal() answers `[409, 'تعذّر تنفيذ الإجراء.']` (:108). `grep -rn "FULFILLMENT_STOPPED|CHARGEBACK_RECORDED|PAYMENT_REVERSED" src supabase/functions` finds nothing.
impact: When M1b-2/M1b-1/M1b-5/M1a land without the matching client round, an operations member marking an order shipped after a chargeback (the very case DB-OPS-02 closes) is told to try again, and retries until he gives up, never learning that the owner stopped the shipment; the owner refusing a refund on a charged-back payment sees a generic failure. The guard holds; the explanation is missing.
proposed_fix: Add the words in the same round as the SQL: REFUSALS.fulfil FULFILLMENT_STOPPED ('أوقف المالك شحن هذا العنصر بعد اعتراض على الدفع.') and REFUND_IN_FLIGHT, REFUSALS.resolve PAYMENT_REVERSED, refunds.ts CHARGEBACK_RECORDED; plus a unit test that every code the migrations return through these functions has an entry (grep the SQL in the test).
prior_overlap: in-flight: wave A rulings M1b-1 (DB-POST-01), M1b-2 (DB-OPS-02), M1b-5 (DB-POST-02), M1a-5b (DB-PAY-06) add the codes; F2b is the client round. No finding names the missing words.

title: The buyer's order page refuses a reply with one key more than it knows, and that reply is built from SQL helpers other features change: one added field blanks every order page
evidence: parseOrderView runs `exact()` (orders.ts:223-228: `!keys.every((key) => required.includes(key) || optional.includes(key))` → malformed) on `order` (:305-320), `payment` (:321), every item (:276-280), its download (:281), preorder (:257), summary line (:263) and return (:298); fetchOrder turns the throw into `{ failure: 'network' }` (:354-357). The `orders` function forwards SQL's objects unfiltered (supabase/functions/_shared/orders.ts:224), and order_access builds `order` as `finance.order_summary(o.id) || {...}` and `payment` as `finance.payment_view(...) - 'orderId' - 'hasToken'` (20261002140000_delivery.sql:102, :112): two helpers shared with checkout and the return page, and order_summary has already been redefined once (20261002110000_checkout_payment.sql:288). The contract asks exactness only of the small replies (P08-CONTRACT.md:482), and quote.ts and the admin parsers ignore extra keys.
impact: A migration that adds a field to order_summary or payment_view for checkout or the return page (or to order_access itself) turns every buyer's /orders page, downloads included, into «تعذّر الاتصال بالخدمة؛ أعد المحاولة.» from the moment `db push` runs until a rebuilt site is deployed and each buyer reloads: database and static site are deployed separately, so there is always such a window, and it is total for that page. The strictness protects nothing at runtime: the extra key has already reached the browser.
proposed_fix: Check required keys only in parseOrderView and its item/payment/return parsers (keep `exact` for the three small replies the contract names); move the 'no unexpected key' guarantee into tests/unit (pin order_access's key set against the parser) so a server-side addition fails CI instead of the live page.

title: OrderView's `act` promises to re-read the order «whatever the answer» but skips it on any error; its copy in ReconciliationView does re-read: a shipment committed behind a lost reply still shows «قيد التجهيز» with «حاول مرة أخرى»
evidence: The doc comment (OrderView.tsx:164-167) says «the order is read again whatever the answer (a refusal may mean it changed)», and moneyRun does so unconditionally (:221). `act` re-reads only on the success path: `const { data, error } = await call(); if (error) { text = error.code === '42501' ? NO_PERMISSION : SAVE_FAILED } else { unread = await reread(...) ...}` (:180-184), and a throw (a malformed reply in parseActionReply) skips it too and says «تعذّر الحفظ» (:193-195). The same scaffolding copied into ReconciliationView routes `act` through `run`, which re-reads both lists in every outcome and answers a malformed reply with BAD_REPLY (ReconciliationView.tsx:150-186). postgrest-js 2.117.1 turns a dropped connection after the request was sent into `{ error: { code: '' } }` (no throw, and a POST is never retried), i.e. the skipped branch.
impact: Operations mark items shipped (or the owner resolves an order / closes a review) on a flaky connection: the SQL commits (the shipped mail is queued), the reply is lost, and the screen keeps the old state with «تعذّر الحفظ. حاول مرة أخرى.» and the carrier fields filled. The retry is then refused as BAD_TRANSITION («لا تنتقل هذه العناصر إلى هذه الحالة.») before the re-read finally shows the truth: two contradictory messages for one successful action, no data harm (the SQL guards the transition).
proposed_fix: Re-read in every outcome, as moneyRun and ReconciliationView's run do: move `unread = await reread(load.detail.order.id)` after the try/catch, and answer a parse failure with BAD_REPLY. Structurally, one hook for the status/alert lines, the in-flight guard and the always-re-read (OrderView, ReconciliationView, VariantCommerce, StatsView each keep a copy) removes this class of drift.

title: Eight room schemas are built at import and never used (one repeats the jewel options by hand), and cart.ts keeps removeLine alive only for its test
evidence: `grep -rn 'jewelSchema|reelMediaSchema|galleryPhotoSchema|builtMovementSchema|thuraFlavourSchema|thuraItemSchema|moonlightCupItemSchema|boutiqueItemSchema' src tests scripts` finds only their declarations (rooms.ts:22, 39, 45, 81, 170, 187, 196, 205). Seven are `schemaFromFields(...)` calls, run on every import of the collection registry (admin bundle and build); `jewelSchema = z.enum(['coral', 'aub', 'saffron', 'paper'])` (:22) copies JEWEL_FIELD.options (:27), the list the real schemas derive from. `removeLine` (src/lib/cart.ts:140) is imported only by tests/unit/cart.test.ts (:41, :141, :339); the cart uses removeLines.
impact: No runtime defect. A maintainer adding a room colour edits JEWEL_FIELD and may also edit the dead jewelSchema (or trust it); eight zod schemas are constructed for nothing on every admin page load.
proposed_fix: Delete the eight unused `*Schema` exports (keep the `*Fields`), and delete removeLine with its two test uses (removeLines covers the cart).
prior_overlap: same class as AUDIT-1 X6.x (fixed items); FIX-A1-01/-03 cover splitCenter and FieldType, not these

title: The cart swallows a failed city list as «no cities»; the checkout's copy of the same loader reports it and offers a retry
evidence: CartView: `fetchCities().then(setCities).catch(() => setCities([]))` (CartView.tsx:116), then renders the select with only «اختر المدينة» (:321-334) and no message or retry. CheckoutForm loads the same list with a three-state `citiesState` ('loading' | 'failed' | 'loaded', :129-130, :188-195), shows «تعذّر تحميل قائمة المدن.» with «أعد المحاولة» on failure (:690-705) and «لا نوصل إلى أي مدينة حاليًا.» only for a list that loaded empty (:500, :706-710). fetchCities itself documents that it throws so that «an empty list means none are served» (quote.ts:396).
impact: A buyer with a physical item whose city request fails (a dropped connection, a Data API blip) sees an empty city menu on /cart and the quote's «اختر مدينة التوصيل.», with nothing saying the list failed and no way to load it again short of reloading the page; the failure is indistinguishable from «we deliver nowhere».
proposed_fix: Give CartView the checkout's three states (or one small shared useCities hook used by both): on failure show «تعذّر تحميل قائمة المدن.» with «أعد المحاولة», as CheckoutForm does.
prior_overlap: none (AUDIT-2 STORE-cart items fixed quote retry, not the city list)

title: The staff order search re-implements the address grammar without the punycode step every server copy applies, so a buyer's Arabic-domain address cannot be searched as he writes it
evidence: Every function that stores or looks up a buyer address normalizes it the same way: `.trim().toLowerCase().max(254).transform((email) => toAsciiAddress(email)).refine(... EMAIL_SHAPE.test ...)`, written out four times (contact.ts:72-79, checkout.ts:74-81, orders.ts:45-51, notify.ts:45-51); toAsciiAddress punycodes a non-ASCII domain (contact.ts:53-68), so `x@مثال.السعودية` is stored as `x@xn--...`. The staff search copies only the grammar: `const EMAIL = /^[a-z0-9._%+-]{1,64}@[a-z0-9.-]{1,190}.(?:[a-z]{2,63}|xn--[a-z0-9-]{2,59})$/i` and `EMAIL.test(query) ? query.toLowerCase() : null` (admin-orders.ts:120, :132); orders_list then hashes that text and compares it with the stored hash (20261007110000_fable_audit_operations.sql:121-136). A sixth copy, the site contact address rule CONTACT_EMAIL_PATTERN (src/admin/collections/site-settings.ts:105), has no xn-- branch at all.
impact: When a buyer with an internationalised address (the Saudi `.السعودية` domain is the case toAsciiAddress was written for) writes to Anas about his order, operations paste his address into «بحث برقم الطلب أو البريد» and get «أدخل رقم طلب كاملًا أو بريدًا إلكترونيًا.»; the order is findable only by its number or by typing the xn-- form. The four server copies agree today, but they must stay byte-identical for link recovery and the search to keep matching checkout's stored hash, and nothing ties them together.
proposed_fix: Move EMAIL_SHAPE, toAsciiAddress and the email field into one pure module next to saudi-mobile.ts (no Deno or supabase-js import), use it in the four functions, and run normalizeOrderQuery's address branch through toAsciiAddress before the grammar check.

title: The owner's step-up is written three times and the two older copies drifted: a failed factor lookup reads as «not enrolled», and the settings copy re-opens the dialog it says it opens once
evidence: The money screens use one helper pair: useStepUp returns 'failed' on a listFactors error (`if (error) return 'failed'`, RefundView.tsx:91-92) and withStepUp sends the call once more and treats a second STEP_UP_REQUIRED as an answer, «never another dialog» (admin-money.ts:249-260). The store settings and the team screen each keep their own copy: `const { data } = await supabase.auth.mfa.listFactors(); const verified = data?.totp.find(...); if (!verified) { setNeedsEnrollment(true) ...` (CommerceSettingsForm.tsx:111-115, TeamView.tsx:84-88) drop the error, and CommerceSettingsForm's onStepUpVerified feeds the retry's reply back into applyResult (:139-141), which opens the dialog again on STEP_UP_REQUIRED (:109-117), against its header «the same save retries exactly once» (:7-8).
impact: When the factor lookup fails (a dropped connection, an Auth hiccup) an owner who has an authenticator is told «يلزم تفعيل تطبيق المصادقة أولًا. اذهب إلى صفحة الأمان.» while saving the seller details, approving the policies, opening the store or changing the team, and may go and enrol a second factor. If the retried save is refused for step-up again, the settings screen asks for another code instead of saying why.
proposed_fix: Replace both local copies with the existing useStepUp + withStepUp (as RefundView and DisputeForm use them), so the three screens share one behaviour: a lookup failure says «تعذّر الاتصال بالخادم.» and a second STEP_UP_REQUIRED is reported, not re-prompted.
prior_overlap: EF-ADMIN-19 (StepUp says «الرمز غير صحيح.» for every failure) is the dialog's own wording; this is the callers' lookup and loop

title: After a successful store-settings action a failed re-read is ignored, so the next action sends the old version and the owner is told another session changed the settings
evidence: applyResult on success: `setSaved(successMessage); const loaded = await loadRow(); if (loaded) setRow(loaded); return` (CommerceSettingsForm.tsx:103-107): a null re-read keeps the old `row`, including `row.version`, and says nothing. Every action sends `expectedVersion: row.version` (:156, :240, :260); the function answers a stale version with 409 «تغيّرت الإعدادات من جلسة أخرى. أعد تحميل الصفحة.» (supabase/functions/_shared/admin.ts:450, :469, :497). The save replies already carry the new version (`ok({ version })`, admin.ts:446, :494) and are discarded.
impact: The owner saves the seller details (the version moves on), the re-read fails on a flaky connection, the screen says «تم الحفظ.»; his next press («اعتماد السياسات المنشورة» or «افتح الشراء») is refused as a change from another session, which never happened. The store can open later than he believes he opened it if he does not notice the refusal.
proposed_fix: Take the version from the action's own reply when it has one (`result.data.version`), and when the re-read fails say so next to the success sentence, as the order screens do with REREAD_FAILED.
prior_overlap: none (FIX-A2-03 is the stale «الشراء مفتوح» after a policy republish, a different staleness)

title: One OTP_LENGTH serves both the email sign-in code and the TOTP, so the planned 8-digit sign-in code (F2a-2) would be cut to 6 digits unless the helper is split
evidence: `const OTP_LENGTH = 6` with the comment «`otp_length` in supabase/config.toml; a TOTP is six too» (digits.ts:1-2), and otpDigits ends `.slice(0, OTP_LENGTH)` (:16). The same function filters the email code (SignIn.tsx:130), the enrolment TOTP (MfaEnroll.tsx:128) and the step-up TOTP (StepUp.tsx:84). The sign-in copy repeats the length in words: «...أرسلنا إليه رمزًا من 6 أرقام.» (SignIn.tsx:12). supabase/config.toml:240 still says `otp_length = 6`; the wave A ruling for CLIENT-SEC-06 schedules an 8-digit code (F2a-2: config, UI, tests).
impact: None today. When F2a-2 raises otp_length to 8, changing only the config and the sentence leaves the sign-in field truncating every typed or pasted code to its first 6 digits, so no staff member can sign in; raising OTP_LENGTH instead lets 8 digits into the TOTP fields. The coupling is invisible from either call site.
proposed_fix: Give otpDigits a length argument (or export emailCodeDigits/totpDigits) and keep the email length next to its sentence; do it in F2a-2.

title: The security page tells the owner the authenticator is needed for team actions only; since P06-P08 it also guards refunds, disputes, the seller details, the policy approval and opening the store
evidence: For an enrolled owner the page says «مطلوب لتفعيل إجراءات الفريق: الدعوة وتغيير الدور والإيقاف.» (MfaEnroll.tsx:105), and its doc comment repeats «step-up for invite, role change and revoke» (:18-21); StepUp's comment says the caller «retries the original `staff-admin` call» (StepUp.tsx:12-13). The `admin` function refuses STEP_UP_REQUIRED for refund-create, refund-record-external, dispute-record, commerce-settings-save, commerce-policies-approve and commerce-checkout-set as well (supabase/functions/_shared/admin.ts:225, 232, 236, 240, 244, 248), besides staff-admin (staff-admin/index.ts:52).
impact: Anas, reading that the authenticator matters only for managing the team, may leave it unenrolled (or remove it from his phone) until the day he must refund a buyer or open the store, when the screen stops him with «يلزم تفعيل تطبيق المصادقة أولًا» in the middle of the money action.
proposed_fix: Name what it guards: «مطلوب للإجراءات الحساسة: الاسترداد وتسجيل النزاعات وبيانات البائع واعتماد السياسات وفتح الشراء وإدارة الفريق.» (wording for the owner), and correct the two comments.

title: Rules and helpers copied by hand between the functions and the admin, identical today with nothing tying them: the Riyadh day (3), the upload limits (2 sets), the file-size words, the preorder sentence
evidence: `riyadhToday` is written three times: admin-money.ts:389 (used by DisputeForm), admin-commerce.ts:55 (used by tables/variants.ts) and supabase/functions/_shared/disputes.ts:44 (the server's bound on a dispute day). MediaUpload.tsx:25-28 restates ORIGINAL_MIME_TYPES, MAX_ORIGINAL_BYTES, MAX_PIXELS and MAX_DERIVATIVE_BYTES of _shared/media.ts:16-25 (its comment says the client «cannot import» that module, while the pure media-rules.ts the client already imports could hold them); admin-commerce.ts:102 restates paid-files.ts:32 PAID_FILE_MAX_BYTES. MediaLibrary.tsx:111-115 formatBytes and admin-commerce.ts:136-138 formatFileSize are the same function. OrderPage.tsx:135 inlines «طلب مسبق: يُسلَّم في ${formatDate(...)}» instead of quote.ts:60 preorderSentence, whose doc says the order page uses the same words.
impact: None today: every pair agrees. Each is a place where a later change to one side (a 20 MiB original, a new paid-file limit, a reworded preorder line) leaves the other side refusing or saying something different, the way the email grammar already drifted in the staff search (QUALITY-08).
proposed_fix: Export riyadhToday once (the pure saudi-mobile.ts-style module under _shared, imported by both libs and disputes.ts); move the four media limits into media-rules.ts and the paid-file limit into a pure module both sides import; keep one formatFileSize; call preorderSentence in OrderPage.
prior_overlap: same family as AUDIT-1 X6.6 (riyadhLocalToIso re-implemented, fixed) and X6.13; these copies are newer (P05-P08)

title: Vestigial code from earlier architectures: a session token kept only as a boolean, a `pg`-era Date branch, and a Worker-era comment
evidence: CollectionForm keeps `accessToken` in state with its own getSession read and onAuthStateChange subscription (CollectionForm.tsx:77, 103-112), and uses it only as `{accessToken && baseSeq > 0 && (<PublishBar ...` (:362): PublishBar takes no token (publishing goes through admin-publish.ts and the shared browser client since D32). outbox.ts:118-122 types `created_at: Date | string` and branches on `contact.created_at instanceof Date`, but the row comes from the Data API rpc as JSON (processRow types it `created_at: string`, :200-205), so the Date branch cannot run. media.ts:168-170 explains dropping `file-type` because «the Worker bundle cannot resolve» strtok3; there has been no Worker since D32. content.ts:288-292 says Picture.tsx reads its own manifest JSON, but Picture now goes through images.ts (Picture.tsx:1).
impact: No runtime defect. The token subscription re-renders the editor on every token refresh and suggests to a maintainer that publishing still depends on the raw token; the comments point maintainers at architectures that no longer exist.
proposed_fix: Gate PublishBar on `baseSeq > 0` alone and drop the token state and subscription (AdminShell already handles a signed-out session); type created_at as string and drop the instanceof branch; correct the two comments.

title: The book reader handles a failed reader chunk and a failed PDF, but not a failed page-flip chunk: the book opens to an empty stage with live-looking controls and no message
evidence: `void import('page-flip').then(({ PageFlip }) => { if (cancelled) return ... flip.loadFromHTML([...elements].reverse()) ...` (PdfBookReader.tsx:286-310) has no rejection handler. The leaves are attached only inside that callback, so on a rejection the stage keeps an empty block, and turn/go return early (`if (!flip || !block) return`, :230). The two other loads of the same open are handled: BookPreview catches the reader chunk (`import('./PdfBookReader').then(..., () => setState('failed'))`, BookPreview.tsx:30-32) and the PDF failure sets `failed` with «تعذّر فتح الصفحات.» and «إعادة المحاولة» (:170-173, :506-528).
impact: A visitor whose connection drops between the reader chunk and the page-flip chunk (the first open of the book on a phone) sees the reader's tools around an empty book: the arrows and the part menu do nothing, nothing says why, and there is no retry; only «عرض للقراءة» (which does not need page-flip) or a reload recovers. The browser logs an unhandled rejection.
proposed_fix: Add the rejection: `.catch(() => { if (!cancelled) setFailed(true) })`, which shows the existing «تعذّر فتح الصفحات.» with «إعادة المحاولة» and the PDF link.
prior_overlap: AUDIT-2 BOOK-4 (a failed or superseded pdf load is destroyed) covered the PDF load, not this import
